decode.scroll_stop_trick: Two arms locked in an arm-wrestle, one thick and veined, one thin and pale, under 'Beef vs. Spaghetti' — the metaphor and the photo say the same thing in half a second.
decode.angle_carried: strength with age: 'made for men who refuse to shrink with age'
decode.hidden_reading: the playground insult (spaghetti arms) — social mechanism: everyone can see which one you are
decode.scene_logic: a contest where the body difference is the whole point. Ours: two men side by side at a backyard BBQ, shirts tucked, belt line in frame — the belly difference is the contest
decode.visual_trick: two bodies touching at the centre, the strong one on the left, dark vignette, product floating top-left — copy literally with two torsos: left a flat tucked-in waist, right a belly hanging over the belt, standing shoulder to shoulder, each holding a beer
decode.shape_or_function_equivalent: thick arm vs thin arm ↔ flat waist vs keg belly; 'Beef vs. Spaghetti' ↔ 'Belt Buckle vs. Keg'
decode.verb_of_the_scene: compete / show off side by side
decode.render_style: photoreal, dark moody background, warm skin, sharp detail
decode.text_treatment: white regular sans top line, white bold line with the brand name in red → Edenvia blue, red footer band → Edenvia navy band with white bold text

strategy.angle: A8-M the man's belly that isn't fat — 'it's not the beer, it's what your body stopped clearing'
strategy.mechanism: M1: when the body can't clear everyday oxidative stress, the tissue in the legs stays inflamed and stops draining normally, so fluid sits there — heavy, tender, puffy — and no diet reaches it, because it was never fat; the tablet turns a glass of water into hydrogen-rich water, hydrogen is the smallest molecule there is, reaches the tissue and helps the body switch that process off so normal drainage can resume
strategy.sub_avatar: trigger: belt on the last hole, the photo at the BBQ · cause: a bloated, fluid-heavy belly no diet moved · tried: cutting beer, sit-ups, keto
strategy.belief_installed: A belly that no diet moves isn't food I stored — it's what my body stopped clearing.
